title: Return on Investment (ROI) Methodology
overview: ROI measures the profitability of an investment relative to its cost. While simple ROI is intuitive, annualized returns and IRR provide better comparisons across different time periods.

methods.name: Simple ROI
methods.description: The basic formula showing total return as a percentage of initial investment. Easy to calculate but doesn't account for time.

formula.name: Simple ROI Formula
formula.expression:
ROI = (Current Value - Cost) / Cost × 100
Or: ROI = (Gain) / Cost × 100

limitations: Can't compare investments of different durations

methods.name: Annualized ROI (CAGR)
methods.description: Compound Annual Growth Rate shows the steady yearly return that would produce the same final result. Better for comparing investments over different time periods.
methods.accuracy: Good for comparing different duration investments

methods.name: Internal Rate of Return (IRR)
methods.description: The discount rate that makes the net present value of all cash flows equal to zero. Essential for investments with multiple cash flows.

formula.name: IRR Calculation
formula.expression:
NPV = Σ (Cash Flow_t / (1 + IRR)^t) = 0
Solve for IRR

methods.accuracy: Most comprehensive for complex cash flows
methods.bestFor: Real estate, business investments with cash flows

methods.name: Total Return (Including Dividends)
methods.description: Includes both price appreciation and income (dividends, interest). Essential for fair comparison of stocks vs bonds.

formula.name: Total Return
formula.expression: Total Return = (End Price - Start Price + Income) / Start Price × 100

limitations: Tax treatment varies by income type

footnotes: After-tax return matters more than pre-tax for taxable accounts
Risk-adjusted return (Sharpe ratio) accounts for volatility
Past performance doesn't guarantee future results
disclaimer: ROI calculations are based on provided data. Investment returns involve risk and can be negative. Consider fees, taxes, and inflation when evaluating investments.
